findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/red-evidence-subsystem-spec.md:1323-1331 (§5.3 Shared classifier) asserts the material hash file set already derives from resolveMaterialCodePolicy ("the material set is whatever that function (post-W1 snapshot policy) hashes", then mandates isMaterialPath be implemented via resolveMaterialCodePolicy and be called by currentMaterialHash). This is false at current HEAD and unsupported by the W1 plan it cites: currentMaterialHash (packages/main/src/core/evidence-freshness.ts:489-508) filters via isMaterialExcludedPath (evidence-freshness.ts:163-165 = isStoryMetadataPath || isMaterialExcludedRuntimeArtifactPath); evidence-freshness.ts never imports resolveMaterialCodePolicy (packages/main/src/core/material-code-policy.ts), which is used only by review-assurance-floor.ts, scope-diff-pack.ts, validate-concept.ts and the language-neutral-gates smoke. The W1 execution plan itself (docs/requirements/decisions/language-neutral-gates-execution-plan.md Change A + §3 Verification: "Three-consumer RED: py/rs/go story flips to required through floor + repro + ProofStory") names exactly three resolveMaterialCodePolicy consumers, not evidence-freshness.ts/currentMaterialHash, so "post-W1 snapshot policy" is not a fact W1 establishes. This also self-contradicts this same spec doc at line 780 (§2.1.2): "W2 does not redefine the material hash; it reuses this function verbatim." Making currentMaterialHash call the proposed isMaterialPath would change its filtering semantics for every existing caller across the codebase, not just red-evidence freshness -- an out-of-W2-scope global behavior change the spec does not flag. An implementer following §5.3 literally has no accurate premise to build isMaterialPath on, or would silently redefine a shared primitive beyond this spec's stated non-goals (§0.3).
